schema_note: Every number in this file is real and reproducible from the files it was computed from -- actual sacrebleu runs, actual verification-pipeline state files, or actual dataset files in the lao-thai-translator repository, which is not public, so a reader outside the project cannot recompute them independently. Nothing here is estimated, projected, or hand-typed as a round number. Fields with a null value mean 'not measured under this methodology,' never 'assumed good.'

generations.label: Generation 3
generations.release_notes: The DPO-trained checkpoint produced by an earlier 5-step sanitization-pipeline retrain. Superseded after we identified what we internally call the 'Generation 3 crisis': a cycle-consistency blind spot where a forward and reverse translation model can share a bias that round-trips cleanly while being confidently wrong about the actual meaning. That specific failure mode is the reason Generation 4's verification system (below) uses back-translation as only one of two independent checks, never the sole gate. We don't show chrF++/BLEU scores for Generation 3 -- it predates this project's current benchmark suites, and we'd rather show nothing than a number we didn't actually measure.

generations.label: Generation 4 (current for "Translated screenplay" files, being replaced)

corrections.counted_over: The 287 films the Back-Translation Consensus verification run covered. Of those, 187 are still published as "Translated screenplay" files, 98 are still in the catalogue but now have a "Subtitles" file instead (their screenplay file was replaced), and 2 are no longer published at all.
defect_categories_fixed: Garbled decoder artifact (a bare "ແມ" token left as an incomplete fragment, never finished into a real word)
Repetition / stutter artifacts (e.g. a phrase's opening words duplicated back-to-back)
"Cat" hallucination (a garbled token completed into the unrelated real word for "cat")
"Interfere" hallucination (the real word for "interfere/intervene" substituted for unrelated content -- the single largest defect pattern found in this project)
Code-mixing (untranslated English words left stranded inside otherwise-Lao sentences)
Numeral errors (e.g. "100 thousand" rendered as "ten thousand")

generations.release_notes: The 287 films in the verification run (187 of them are still published as "Translated screenplay" files, 98 are still in the catalogue but now have a "Subtitles" file instead, and 2 are no longer published) were re-checked automatically by two machine filters -- no human reviewer read or approved these translations. Filter 1 is a set of deterministic Lao-text pattern checks built and refined by hand as each new failure pattern was found. Filter 2 is an English-only back-translation semantic-equivalence judge: the candidate Lao line is translated back into English by a separate reverse-direction model and a local LLM running on the project's own computer is asked only whether the two English sentences mean the same thing -- the model is never shown Lao to grade, precisely because that self-referential check is what caused the Generation 3 crisis. An automatic correction was applied only when both filters independently approved it. Re-summed from the run's own per-film state file on 2026-09-29: 7,263 corrections across all 287 films, of which 4,479 are in the 187 files still published. Earlier versions of this page showed 7,251 and then 7,231 for the run as a whole; both were counted at an earlier point and are superseded by this re-sum, which comes straight from the state file named above. The largest single defect found was a hallucinated substitution of the real Lao word for 'interfere' standing in for unrelated content -- 654 raw occurrences found corpus-wide; a dedicated cleanup pass fixed only 15 of those (2.6%), confirming most instances are a stable model bias rather than a one-off translation slip. That known limitation is left undisturbed in the published corpus rather than papered over, pending a future targeted retrain. The corrections this run found were not used to train either model in use here: the retraining planned on them was dropped before it started (see Generation 5 below), and the training file behind S3X, lao_nlp/external_corpora/S3x1_heldout.jsonl, records the file each of its 206,745 rows came from -- none of them the corrections file, whose rows were written a week after that training set's movie corpus. Separately, the review step that produced the published files sent lines to Google Gemini, a cloud AI service, and applied some of its edits; that step will not be used again. The model was fine-tuned mostly on machine-translated text, including earlier output of this project and corrections written by Google Gemini; only a small share of its training data was translated by people.

generations.label: Generation 5 (retired plan)
generations.release_notes: This DPO/self-training plan was abandoned; training was never started. The staged dataset numbers below are kept as a historical record only. The next candidate under evaluation is a supervised adapter (S3X), to be checked by a native Lao reader before any use. We publish performance numbers only after they're actually measured against a trained, evaluated checkpoint -- this entry intentionally has no scores yet.

generations.label: S3X (current for "Subtitles" files)
generations.release_notes: S3X is a supervised (non-DPO) LoRA adapter fine-tuned on NLLB-200 1.3B. It is used for every file on this site labeled "Subtitles": real, timed English subtitle files translated directly, with no cloud AI review step (no Google Gemini pass, unlike the older "Translated screenplay" files) and no find-and-replace rule-table post-processing. Files still labeled "Translated screenplay" are Generation 4 output and are being replaced by real subtitle-timed "Subtitles" files as they become available. Like every generation on this page, S3X was fine-tuned mostly on machine-translated text, including earlier output of this project and corrections written by Google Gemini; only a small share of its training data was translated by people -- a fact about training data, not about how S3X's own output is produced or reviewed. No quality score is published for S3X: no native Lao reader has reviewed it yet, and this project does not publish a result before it is actually measured (see the Quality Score section).
